messages:
Marta: Heads-up: noticed a perf regression on the reranker/embeddings non-chat endpoint after the kernel-selector tweak. p95 up ~18% and throughput more variable. Looks like batching behavior changed and KV cache is getting thrashed.

perf-bot: ALERT: reranker-vec-prod p95 latency +18% detected at 2026-03-17T09:12Z. Traces available.

Devin: can you paste the profiling snapshot and kernel selection logs? timeline + selector decisions will help root cause.

Marta: quick flame summary from staging run: 
```
cpu: batching thread
- continuous_batcher::form_batch 36%
- kernel_selector::pick_kernel 27% (many fallbacks)
- kv_cache::evict_or_merge 14%
- matmul_slow_path 13%
- postproc/serialize 10%
```
Seeing an uptick where the selector picks slower kernels for short sequences -> more matmul slow path and KV rematerialization.

Akshay: my hunch: short non-chat requests are creating small batches that push the selector into scalar/slow matmul paths, plus cold KV entries cause re-materialize which amplifies cost.

Marta: staging request size distribution: 60% <=16 tokens, 30% 17-64, 10% >64. Current batcher forms 4-8 item batches with formation_window_ms=5 which used to be okay pre-selector change.

Devin: two quick knobs to try: (1) prefer token budget when forming batches (increase token_budget_target), (2) prefer warm-kv items earlier in a batch to avoid cold misses.

Samir: propose experiments to run on staging: 
A) formation_window_ms=12, token_budget_target=3500
B) formation_window_ms=8, token_budget_target=2500, prefer_warm_kv=true
C) revert the selector threshold that caused fallback for short sequences (safety rollback)
Will run each 30m with realistic short-request noise and collect p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_fallback_ratio, CPU/GPU util.

Akshay: also instrument metrics: "kv_cache_hit_ratio_by_batch" and "kernel_fallback_ratio" so we can correlate cache behavior with kernel choices.

Marta: draft batcher config for quick patch (WIP):
```
batcher:
  formation_window_ms: 12
  max_items: 64
  token_budget_target: 3500
  prefer_warm_kv: true
  allow_mixed_kernels: false  # prefer homogeneous kernel per batch
```

Devin: allow_mixed_kernels=false should prevent mid-batch kernel churn. Might increase head-of-line wait but could reduce fallback overhead and per-batch kernel switching cost.

Akshay: one more nuance: mixed quantization targets across items can force selector to choose slower stable kernels. Add a pre-check to detect mixed quant-compatibility and prefer the stable kernel for the whole batch.

Samir: scheduling: start experiments 2026-03-18T03:00Z UTC. I'll run A/B/C, collect traces, and upload to this thread.

Marta: action items: 
- @Samir run experiments and upload perf traces
- @Devin add metrics (kv_cache_hit_ratio_by_batch, kernel_fallback_ratio) and dashboards
- @Akshay prepare rollback/selector-patch if C shows improvement
- @Marta create canary rollout plan for Dedicated cluster ensuring flags match hosted/staging

Devin: quick local repro script to generate short-shot noise: 
```
# reproduce small-batch fallback locally
for i in range(0,1000):
  send_request(tokens=random.randint(1,16))
  sleep(random.uniform(0.001, 0.02))
```

Ops-bot: reminder: ensure Dedicated uses the same kernel selector flags; avoid config drift between environments. Include configs in canary PR.

Marta: good point. I'll include config diffs and let deploy-bot gate the canary.

Akshay: if prefer_warm_kv reduces fallback_ratio by >50% and p95 improves noticeably, we should consider keeping allow_mixed_kernels=false for rerank/embedding endpoints.

Samir: created run ticket, grabbing baseline now. Will post results here after runs. :white_check_mark:

Devin: if any customer impact emerges, escalate on #incidents and tag eng-oncall.

Marta: thanks all. Plan is to try low-risk batch/kv policy tuning first before changing kernel heuristics. Will report back after Samir's experiments.
